## Natural history notes

A native perennial herb in the rockrose family characterized by slender branching stems, narrow leaves, and numerous tiny reddish-brown to greenish flowers that develop along delicate inflorescences. Deckert’s Pinweed occurs mainly in dry, sandy upland habitats, especially scrub and scrubby flatwoods, where it grows in open areas with sparse vegetation. Its native range is restricted to the southeastern United States, particularly Florida and Georgia, and it is considered critically imperiled in South Florida. The species is strongly associated with relatively intact, fire-maintained sandy habitats and has a high coefficient of conservatism, reflecting its affinity for high-quality natural communities.
